cars.generation: Original HK2 Facel II production-road GT family
cars.variant: 6.3-litre manual architecture — HK2 B109, Chicane 4/2011 road reference
cars.specification_market: Architecture reference HK2 B109 as driven in Chicane Magazine 4/2011, not a claim of unchanged factory condition. The article covers a modern electric steering conversion and corrected alignment: neither is original equipment or unmodified factory handling. Its 390-pk/5500-rpm, approximate speed/weight and production figures are not imported. 1962 identifies the start of the stated 1962–1964 model range, not a verified build year for B109. Other engines, transmissions and years add no counts.
cars.summary: The Facel II is a significant French-American performance GT, combining Chrysler V8 power with a distinctive low French coupe body. First-hand road driving documents forceful acceleration and sustained touring ability. Its place in postwar GT history supports one original family entry; rarity, luxury and a fastest-coupe slogan do not establish admission by themselves.

facts.title: HK2 identity
facts.explanation: The Amicale identifies the Facel II as type HK2, presented at Paris in October 1961 as the successor to the earlier FV/HK500 line. That model identity is distinct from the separately described modern steering work on the road-feature car.

cars.generation: Original XPower SV / SV-R production-road sports-coupe family
cars.variant: Entry-level 4.6 V8 five-speed manual — 29 October 2003 launch specification
cars.specification_market: 29 October 2003 manufacturer launch release, initial entry-level manual SV specification. Retains native 320 hp SAE and 410 Nm without adopting the inconsistent 230 kW conversion. Estimated acceleration/speed and inconsistent mph/km/h pairs, 765-hp Bonneville proposal, 2002 X80 show-car figures, later SV-R 5.0 engine, automatic and post-administration upgrades are excluded. One original SV/SV-R family; no extra trim, engine or completion-year counts.
cars.summary: The XPower SV was MG’s ambitious carbon-bodied V8 flagship, pairing a steel box frame and integrated rollover structure with a rear-drive sports-car layout. Its engineering and distinctive place in MG’s performance history justify one original family entry. A long-term SV-R road test records involving handling and braking alongside substantial finish and reliability shortcomings, rather than establishing merit through rarity alone.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The XPower SV was MG’s ambitious carbon-bodied V8 flagship, pairing a steel box frame and integrated rollover structure with a rear-drive sports-car layout. Its engineering and distinctive place in MG’s performance history justify one original family entry. A long-term SV-R road test records involving handling and braking alongside substantial finish and reliability shortcomings, rather than establishing merit through rarity alone.
